note:
LongMemEval's deterministic retrieval tier (EVAL-3, ADR-0061 decision 5) — `make eval-longmemeval`. Its own file for the reason decision 6 gives: this suite grades a different predicate from the four `evals/baseline.json` carries. Those ask what a block did with a corpus this repository wrote; this one asks whether a block bound the evidence sessions somebody else's benchmark names, over a corpus that is fetched rather than committed and identified in every report by its BLAKE3.

This file is deliberately thin, and the empty space is the honest part. Only the invariants are bounded, because a quality floor written before anything measured the product against this corpus would be a number somebody invented. The floors land with `--update-baseline` after the first run against the real LongMemEval, and that diff is the one to review — it is the first externally-comparable quality claim this product makes.

longmemeval_unattributed_records is zero-tolerance and is not a quality axis: it counts records the block served that the ids-shaped join could not attribute to any session this run seeded. A join that lost records would shrink its own denominator and report the loss as recall, so this is the same class of gate as hallucination_rate — a correctness invariant of the measurement, not a measurement of the product.

longmemeval_bound_instances is the second invariant and it is the axis to read before any recall number here, because it says whether the recall measured retrieval at all. A block that carried every session of its haystack made no ranking decision, so its perfect recall is a statement about the budget. This is not a quality floor either: below half, the run measured composition capacity and its recall should not be published. The first end-to-end run of this suite — four instances of a synthetic corpus with six-session haystacks — scored longmemeval_retrieval_recall 1.0 and longmemeval_bound_instances 0.0, and this gate is what said so out loud. Real instances are ~40 sessions and ~400 turns, where a budget binds.

Two axes are reported and bounded by nothing on purpose. longmemeval_abstention_empty_blocks was decision 10's claim under measurement — that ADR predicted the abstention instances are gradeable at this tier because "the correct block binds nothing". It measured 0.0 on that first run, the decision is amended (ADR-0061, 2026-08-08), and abstention is graded at the model-judged tier instead. The axis stays because it is now evidence for a different question: a composition change that ever does empty an abstention block is a product change worth seeing. longmemeval_latency_p95_ms is a shape detector and emphatically not an SLO — EVAL-6 owns percentile SLOs under load.
